observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: Receiver is read from ECX at 0x00bb9af0 (8b 41 5c), the single argument is read from the stack at ESP+0x4 (0x00bb9af3, 23 44 24 04), and the function terminates with RET 0x4 (0x00bb9afd, c2 04 00) which pops that one argument. Callee-cleaned one-dword stack argument plus an ECX receiver is __thiscall on x86-32. Corroborated at 0x00ba6c3e: PUSH 0x20000 ; MOV ECX,EDI ; CALL 0x00bb9af0 with no caller-side ESP adjustment.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: true iff at least one bit selected by `mask` is set in the receiver's +0x5C dword; the result is exactly 0 or 1, never a mask value
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x00bb9af7 NEG EAX sets CF from the operand's sign, 0x00bb9af9 SBB EAX,EAX yields 0 (CF clear) or 0xFFFFFFFF (CF set), and 0x00bb9afb NEG EAX maps those to 0 and 1. The full dword is therefore written and bits 8..31 are zero. Every consumer tests AL, never the full dword.
observed_original_abi.hidden_receiver: unread by the mask itself; the receiver's +0x5C field IS read, so the receiver must be non-null

semantic_contract: The function answers a single question about a Simulator star-system record: is any bit selected by the caller's 32-bit mask currently set in the record's +0x5C flag word? It reads exactly two dwords - the receiver's flag word and the caller's mask - intersects them, and normalises the result to the boolean 0 or 1 with the NEG/SBB/NEG idiom, so the answer is never a mask value, never a count and never negative. It has no side effects, no callees, no frame, no branches and no error path; a null receiver faults, but a receiver with any flag word value including 0 and 0xFFFFFFFF is legal. Semantics of the mask: it is a bitwise ANY, not an ALL, because the only combination performed is AND followed by a zero test. Callers observed use single-bit masks (0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x100, 0x20000) to ask one flag question at a time, often as a fallback chain, and always consume the answer as an AL predicate. The complementary write path is 0x00bb9b00, which sets or clears the same bits in the same word, and 0x00bb9b30 forces bit 13, so the field is a genuine bit set rather than a scalar.
classification_rationale: Every element the vocabulary requires is read directly from the binary: the complete six-instruction body, the __thiscall ABI (ECX receiver, one callee-cleaned stack dword, RET 0x4), the single field offset 0x5C with the instruction that proves it, the absence of constants beyond the two displacements, the absence of control flow, the absence of callees and the absence of globals. The receiver identity is corroborated six independent ways - the SDK's declared offsets for mType/mTechLevel/field_50/mCitizenSpeciesKey/mPlanets are all hit by distinct sibling accessors, the SDK's own address range 0xBB9870-0xBBA900 contains this function, and Ghidra already carries a named cStarRecord method in the same file that reads the same +0x5C word. The behavioural claim carries no remaining uncertainty: the mask semantics, the result domain, the branch-free structure and the read-only nature are all fixed by the six instructions. The only thing not established is the per-bit MEANING, which is a naming gap and not a behavioural one, so it is listed under unresolved_questions rather than used to lower the classification.
semantic_findings: The whole contract is `(star->mFlags & mask) != 0`. Two dword reads, one AND, one zero test, no side effects.
The result domain is exactly {0, 1}: NEG/SBB/NEG cannot produce a mask value, a count or a negative number, so callers may safely treat the full EAX as a boolean.
The mask semantics is ANY, not ALL, because the only combination is AND then zero-test.
The receiver is Simulator::cStarRecord and the field is mFlags, established by six independent SDK-offset coincidences plus the SDK's own address-range containment, not by a single match.
0x00bb9b00 sixteen bytes later is the exact complement: it ORs or ANDs the same mask into the same word, so the pair is a probe/mutate pair and proves the word is a bit set.
0x00bb9b30 and 0x00bb9b50 apply the same AND-complement/OR idiom to +0x5C and +0x2C respectively, so the record carries at least two independent bit-mask words.
0x00bba900, which Ghidra already names Simulator__cStarRecord__GetPlanetRecords, reads bit 12 of the same +0x5C word directly, and 0x00bbac99 shifts the same word by 0xF to read bit 15.

Callers use single-bit masks exclusively in the five inspected cases, and two of them (0x00bb2070, 0x00bb21b0) form fallback chains that probe several bits in sequence - a shape characteristic of a bitfield queried one flag at a time rather than a general-purpose predicate.
The function is not a vtable entry in any table located by this batch; it is reached exclusively by direct CALL, so its 'interface method' status is unestablished.
unresolved_questions: What does each individual bit of mFlags mean? Bits 0, 1, 2, 8, 13, 17 and 31 were observed at callsites, but no flag name was established for any of them. Spore-ModAPI's own comment on this field ('TODO 1 << 4 (16) is visited?') shows the upstream project has not settled the bit assignment either.
Is this function reachable through a vtable? Every observed call is a direct CALL and no table slot was located for 0x00bb9af0, so its interface status, if any, is unestablished.

Why is the return value computed with NEG/SBB/NEG rather than a SETNE? Both produce 0/1, so the behaviour is identical; the choice is a codegen artefact and carries no semantic content. Recorded so the byte sequence is not mistaken for three meaningful operations.
Does any caller pass a multi-bit mask? The AND would handle it as ANY, but all five inspected callsites pass a single bit, so multi-bit use is supported by the body and unconfirmed by any caller.

The briefing's canonical ledger recorded caller_count 20; the live query also returns 20 caller functions but 25 call sites, because 0x00ba6f20, 0x00b96d40 and 0x00bb2070/0x00bb21b0 call it more than once. The fan-in figure is not a contradiction, only a different counting convention.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has ever been captured for this function; the original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run. Every claim here is static.
A runtime differential test would have to confirm the flag word's value for a known star system, which is the only way to attach a meaning to individual bits.
Because the function dereferences ECX with no null check, a runtime test that passes a null receiver would fault; that is a property of the original and must be preserved, not defended against.

the receiver is dereferenced without a null check
